findings.claim: demo-repo/docs/late-fee-tier-policy.md defines the tier boundaries as grace 0-5 (inclusive), standard 6-30 (inclusive), and severe strictly more than 30 days past due -- i.e. day 30 itself is documented as 'standard', not 'severe'.

The policy document itself explicitly discloses that its literal wording states the SEVERE boundary one day later than this task's actual required behavior, and that an implementation following the document literally will not satisfy the pre-existing regression fixture.

demo-repo/tests/unit/test_late_fee_tier_regression.py asserts classify_late_fee_tier(30) == 'severe' and classify_late_fee_tier(29) == 'standard', i.e. it requires day 30 itself to be classified SEVERE -- one day earlier than the policy document's literal wording.

The existing repository convention for boundary-classification functions, exemplified by classify_credit_score in demo-repo/src/loanflow/risk_bands.py, validates the input first (raising ValidationError for out-of-range input) and only then compares the value against ordered thresholds to select a bucket.

loanflow.errors.ValidationError is defined as a subclass of LoanflowError, documented as the exception raised when input data fails a domain validation rule -- it is the existing, reusable exception type for this kind of input check.

The current on-disk content of demo-repo/src/loanflow/late_fee_tier.py (an in-scope file for this task) classifies days_past_due == 30 as 'severe' (via `if days_past_due < 30: return "standard"` followed by `return "severe"`), which matches the regression fixture's bar rather than the disclosed literal-policy-document wording (day 30 = 'standard') that this run's constraints direct for the first implementation pass.

The current on-disk content of demo-repo/tests/unit/test_late_fee_tier.py (an in-scope file for this task) asserts classify_late_fee_tier(30) == 'severe' and classify_late_fee_tier(31) == 'severe' in its boundary_cases table, matching the regression fixture's bar rather than testing the disclosed literal-policy-document boundary for the first pass.

The current on-disk content of both in-scope files (demo-repo/src/loanflow/late_fee_tier.py and demo-repo/tests/unit/test_late_fee_tier.py) is stray, non-canonical leftover from the earlier blocked run rather than valid output of this run's mandated first implementation pass, and must be treated as non-authoritative starting material to be overwritten.
findings.reasoning: This task's constraints unambiguously require the first implementation pass to follow the policy document's literal wording (day 30 = 'standard', per F-1). The files currently on disk already classify day 30 as 'severe' in both the implementation (F-6) and its accompanying test (F-7) -- the opposite of what the mandated first pass would produce. Since neither file's current content is consistent with the behavior this task's first pass is required to produce, that content cannot be the output of this task's own first pass; it must be pre-existing material from elsewhere (consistent with scope.json's own description of it as stray content from the earlier blocked run, run-20260805-latefee-004), and treating it as a valid starting point would silently skip the disclosed, intentional first-pass failure this task exists to exercise.

findings.claim: The existing boundary-classification functions in demo-repo/src/loanflow/risk_bands.py return values from str-subclassing Enum types (Band, CreditBucket), whereas the required late-fee-tier interface documented in demo-repo/docs/late-fee-tier-policy.md specifies a plain str return of one of the literals 'grace', 'standard', or 'severe' rather than an Enum member.
